proposals.preferred_label: the child remains on a gluten-containing diet during initial celiac serology
proposals.learner_decision: For a child at least two years old with suspected celiac disease, order tTG-IgA with total IgA while the child is eating gluten and refer a positive screen for specialist confirmation before starting a gluten-free diet.
approved_evidence_propositions: Initial testing for suspected celiac disease at age two or older uses tTG-IgA with total IgA on a gluten-containing diet; a positive screen requires confirmation and a gluten-free diet should not begin before diagnostic testing.

normalization_result.normalized_label: the child remains on a gluten containing diet during initial celiac serology

proposals.preferred_label: a febrile child has a measles-compatible respiratory prodrome and rash
proposals.learner_decision: When measles is suspected in a febrile child with compatible respiratory symptoms and rash, institute airborne isolation immediately and report the suspected case to the local public health authority while confirmatory testing is arranged.
approved_evidence_propositions: Measles is airborne; suspected cases require immediate isolation and health professionals must report suspected cases to local public health.

normalization_result.normalized_label: a febrile child has a measles compatible respiratory prodrome and rash

proposals.preferred_label: a newborn has clinically apparent jaundice
proposals.learner_decision: Measure TSB or TcB without delay in a newborn with clinically apparent jaundice and interpret the result against age-in-hours, gestational age, and neurotoxicity-risk thresholds to decide on treatment and follow-up.
approved_evidence_propositions: Visible or suspected significant neonatal jaundice requires prompt bilirubin measurement; treatment and follow-up depend on an hour-specific threshold modified by gestational age and neurotoxicity risk.

normalization_result.normalized_label: a newborn has clinically apparent jaundice

proposals.preferred_label: the patient has symptomatic vaginal discharge
proposals.learner_decision: In a patient with symptomatic vaginal discharge, use the history, examination, vaginal pH and indicated microscopy or molecular testing to distinguish bacterial vaginosis, vulvovaginal candidiasis, and trichomoniasis before selecting organism-specific treatment.
approved_evidence_propositions: Bacterial vaginosis, vulvovaginal candidiasis, and trichomoniasis are common infectious causes of vaginal discharge and should be differentiated with clinical and laboratory findings before targeted management.

normalization_result.normalized_label: the patient has symptomatic vaginal discharge

proposals.preferred_label: prospective daily charting shows symptoms confined to the premenstrual phase across cycles
proposals.learner_decision: Confirm suspected PMS or PMDD with prospective daily symptom charting across menstrual cycles and distinguish it from continuous psychiatric symptoms or premenstrual exacerbation before initiating syndrome-specific treatment.
approved_evidence_propositions: Prospective daily symptom charting is required to establish cyclical timing and distinguish PMS or PMDD from situational disorders and premenstrual exacerbation of another disorder.

normalization_result.normalized_label: prospective daily charting shows symptoms confined to the premenstrual phase across cycles

proposals.learner_decision: Treat suspected esophageal perforation as a surgical emergency: stop oral intake, begin broad-spectrum antimicrobial and resuscitative therapy, obtain urgent specialist source-control assessment, and avoid delaying operative management when indicated.
approved_evidence_propositions: Suspected esophageal perforation requires NPO status, broad-spectrum antibiotics, resuscitation, and urgent source-control assessment; delayed indicated surgery worsens outcomes.

proposals.preferred_label: acute cholecystitis is mild and the patient is a suitable operative candidate
proposals.learner_decision: Initiate antibiotics and supportive care for acute cholecystitis and select early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for a suitable patient with mild disease, modifying source control according to severity and operative risk.
approved_evidence_propositions: Canadian acute-care guidance recommends antibiotics and supportive care initially and includes early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for suitable mild acute cholecystitis, with other approaches for greater severity or risk.

normalization_result.normalized_label: acute cholecystitis is mild and the patient is a suitable operative candidate

proposals.preferred_label: the patient has acute painless monocular vision loss
proposals.learner_decision: Recognize acute painless monocular vision loss from suspected retinal arterial ischemia as a stroke-equivalent emergency and arrange immediate stroke-centre assessment rather than routine outpatient ophthalmology follow-up.
approved_evidence_propositions: Retinal ischemic injury is an ischemic stroke; acute symptomatic retinal artery occlusion warrants immediate stroke-centre referral for systemic evaluation and possible acute intervention.

normalization_result.normalized_label: the patient has acute painless monocular vision loss

proposals.preferred_label: psychosis persists for at least two weeks without prominent mood symptoms
proposals.learner_decision: Diagnose schizoaffective disorder when a mood episode occurs with schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis, mood symptoms occupy a substantial portion of the illness, and psychosis has persisted for at least two weeks without prominent mood symptoms.
approved_evidence_propositions: Schizoaffective disorder requires concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms plus at least two weeks of psychosis without prominent mood symptoms, with mood symptoms present for a substantial illness duration.

normalization_result.normalized_label: psychosis persists for at least two weeks without prominent mood symptoms

proposals.preferred_label: perceived barriers are limiting preventive-health action
proposals.learner_decision: Use the Health Belief Model to identify whether perceived susceptibility and severity, expected benefit, or perceived barriers are limiting a patient's preventive-health behaviour and tailor counselling to the limiting construct.
approved_evidence_propositions: The Health Belief Model links preventive action to perceived susceptibility and severity, perceived effectiveness or benefit, and psychological, financial, or other barriers.

normalization_result.normalized_label: perceived barriers are limiting preventive health action

proposals.preferred_label: duty, breach, harm, and causation are all established
proposals.learner_decision: Recognize that a negligence claim in a common-law Canadian jurisdiction requires duty of care, breach of the reasonable standard of care, patient harm, and a causal connection between the breach and harm; an adverse outcome alone is insufficient.
approved_evidence_propositions: Medical negligence in common-law Canada requires duty, breach, harm, and causation, and the standard is reasonable care rather than perfection.

normalization_result.normalized_label: duty breach harm and causation are all established

proposals.preferred_label: participants are randomly allocated to intervention and control groups
proposals.learner_decision: Identify random allocation to intervention and control groups as the design feature that best balances measured and unmeasured confounders, while recognizing that blinding instead reduces expectation-related measurement bias.
approved_evidence_propositions: Random allocation is the most attractive design-stage control for confounding because it tends to balance characteristics; blinding addresses participant and assessor expectation bias rather than confounding.

normalization_result.normalized_label: participants are randomly allocated to intervention and control groups
